source.scope: Source-aligned argument for irrational_sqrt_two and its square criteria. Edges summarize selected proof steps and source references.

nodes.name: irrational_sqrt_two
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational (√2) := by
  simpa using Nat.prime_two.irrational_sqrt

nodes.name: Square the rational witness
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonneg {q : ℚ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) :
    Irrational (√q) ↔ ¬IsSquare q := by
  refine Iff.not (?_ : Exists _ ↔ Exists _)
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
    refine ⟨y, Rat.cast_injective (α := ℝ) ?_⟩
    rw [Rat.cast_mul, hy, mul_self_sqrt (Rat.cast_nonneg.2 hq)]
  · rintro ⟨q', rfl⟩
    exact ⟨|q'|, mod_cast (sqrt_mul_self_eq_abs q').symm⟩

nodes.name: Transfer squarehood to ℕ
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff {n : ℕ} : Irrational (√n) ↔ ¬IsSquare n := by
  rw [← Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff, ← irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonneg n.cast_nonneg,
    Rat.cast_natCast]

nodes.name: A prime is not a square
nodes.lean:
theorem Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) : Irrational (√p) :=
  irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.mpr hp.not_isSquare

nodes.name: Specialize at two
nodes.lean:
theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational (√2) := by
  simpa using Nat.prime_two.irrational_sqrt

lean:irrational_sqrt_two.title: Irrationality of √2
lean:irrational_sqrt_two.summary: The nonnegative real square root of 2 cannot be represented by a rational number. This follows from the irrationality of prime square roots and the primality of 2.
lean:irrational_sqrt_two.why_here: It is the theorem established by the final specialization.

fact:rational-square.title: Rational square criterion
fact:rational-square.summary: For a nonnegative rational number, rationality of its real square root is equivalent to having a rational square witness. A rational square root itself gives a witness, and a rational square witness gives the square root after taking its absolute value. Negating this equivalence gives the irrationality criterion.
fact:rational-square.statement_latex: \forall q\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0},\quad \sqrt q\notin\mathbb Q\iff\neg\exists r\in\mathbb Q\;(r^2=q),\quad\text{where }\sqrt q\text{ is taken in }\mathbb R.
fact:rational-square.why_here: It supplies the criterion that is then applied to a natural number viewed as rational.

fact:natural-square.title: Natural square criterion
fact:natural-square.summary: A natural number has an irrational real square root exactly when it is not a perfect square in the natural numbers. The transfer works because a natural number that is a square in the rationals is already a square in the naturals.
fact:natural-square.statement_latex: \forall n\in\mathbb N,\quad \sqrt n\notin\mathbb Q\iff\neg\exists m\in\mathbb N\;(m^2=n),\quad\text{where }\sqrt n\text{ is taken in }\mathbb R.
fact:natural-square.why_here: It converts the nonsquare property of a prime into irrationality of its square root.

step:rational-square.title: Match rational square witnesses
step:rational-square.summary: For a nonnegative rational q, suppose a rational y represents its real square root. Squaring gives y² = q in the reals, and injectivity of the rational embedding gives the same equality in the rationals. Conversely, if r² = q for a rational r, then the real square root is |r|, which is rational. Negating the resulting equivalence gives the rational square criterion.
step:rational-square.why_here: It expands irrationality into the absence of a rational representative and derives the rational square criterion.

step:natural-square.title: Transfer squarehood to the naturals
step:natural-square.summary: Apply the rational criterion to a natural number viewed as a nonnegative rational. The squarehood transfer theorem equates having a rational square witness with having a natural square witness. The two embeddings into the reals give the same radicand, so the resulting criterion concerns the original real square root.
step:natural-square.why_here: It turns the rational criterion into one about natural perfect squares.

step:prime-root.title: Prime square roots are irrational
step:prime-root.summary: Start with a prime natural number p. The nonsquare property of irreducibles rules out p = m², since a square of a nonunit factors into two nonunits and a square of a unit is a unit. The natural square criterion then gives irrationality of √p.
step:prime-root.why_here: It supplies the general implication that the final step uses at 2.

fact:specialize.title: Irrationality of √2
fact:specialize.summary: The prime square root theorem at the prime 2 yields the same irrationality statement as the root theorem.
fact:specialize.why_here: It is the explicit conclusion produced by specializing the prime square root theorem.

lean:Irrational.title: Irrationality
lean:Irrational.summary: A real number is irrational when it lies outside the image of the rationals in the reals. Thus a rational representative is a witness to the negation of irrationality.
lean:Irrational.why_here: Its definition lets the rational criterion be proved by comparing two kinds of witnesses.

lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.title: Rational square criterion
lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.summary: For a nonnegative rational q, the real square root of q is irrational exactly when q has no rational square witness.
lean:irrational_sqrt_ratCast_iff_of_nonn.why_here: It is the declaration whose witness argument is summarized in the graph.

lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.title: Squarehood of naturals in ℚ
lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.summary: A natural number is a rational square exactly when it is a natural square. If a reduced fraction a/b with b positive has an integer square, then b² divides a². Coprimality forces b = 1, so the absolute value of the numerator gives a natural witness.
lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.statement_latex: \forall n\in\mathbb N,\quad (\exists r\in\mathbb Q\;r^2=n)\iff(\exists m\in\mathbb N\;m^2=n),\quad\text{with }n\text{ embedded in }\mathbb Q\text{ on the left}.
lean:Rat.isSquare_natCast_iff.why_here: It justifies replacing rational squarehood with natural squarehood for a natural radicand.

lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.title: Natural square criterion
lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.summary: For a natural number n, its real square root is irrational exactly when no natural number squares to n.
lean:irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff.why_here: The graph summarizes its derivation from the rational criterion and applies it to primes.

lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.title: Irrationality of prime square roots
lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.summary: Every prime natural number has an irrational real square root.
lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.statement_latex: \forall p\in\mathbb N,\quad \operatorname{Prime}(p)\Rightarrow\sqrt p\notin\mathbb Q,\quad\text{where }\sqrt p\text{ is taken in }\mathbb R.
lean:Nat.Prime.irrational_sqrt.why_here: This is the general theorem applied at 2 in the final step.

lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.title: Irreducibles are nonsquares
lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.summary: In the natural-number application, a prime is irreducible. If it were a square, its square factorization would force the repeated factor to be a unit, which would make the square itself a unit and contradict irreducibility.
lean:Irreducible.not_isSquare.why_here: It supplies the nonsquare premise for applying the natural square criterion to a prime.

lean:Nat.prime_two.title: Primality of 2
lean:Nat.prime_two.summary: The natural number 2 has exactly the positive divisors 1 and 2.
lean:Nat.prime_two.why_here: This declaration supplies the primality fact needed for the specialization.

fact:prime-root.title: Irrationality of prime square roots
fact:prime-root.summary: If p is a prime natural number, then its real square root is irrational. The result applies to any prime p.
fact:prime-root.why_here: It provides the general premise for the argument at 2.

step:two-prime.title: Invoke the primality of 2
step:two-prime.summary: Use the established theorem that 2 is prime. This supplies the concrete primality premise for the final application.
step:two-prime.why_here: It brings the cited primality theorem into the argument as a premise.

fact:two-prime.title: Primality of 2
fact:two-prime.summary: The required primality condition holds for the specific radicand 2.
fact:two-prime.why_here: It discharges the prime square root theorem's hypothesis at 2.

step:specialize.title: Apply the prime square root theorem
step:specialize.summary: Take p = 2 in the theorem that prime natural numbers have irrational real square roots. Since 2 is prime, the resulting instance gives the irrationality of √2.
step:specialize.why_here: It combines the general prime result and the specific primality fact to obtain the conclusion.

concepts.title: Irrational numbers
concepts.summary: A real number is irrational if no rational number represents it under the usual embedding into the reals.

concepts.title: Square witnesses
concepts.summary: For S equal to ℚ or ℕ, the predicate Sqₛ(x) means that some y in S satisfies y² = x. When a natural number is tested for squarehood in ℚ, it is first viewed as a rational number.

concepts.title: Nonnegative real square root
concepts.summary: For a nonnegative real x, its square root is the unique nonnegative real whose square is x. In particular, √(r²) = |r| for real r.

concepts.title: Squarehood across ℕ and ℚ
concepts.summary: A natural number has a square witness in ℚ exactly when it has one in ℕ. A rational witness whose square is an integer has denominator 1 in lowest terms.

concepts.title: Primes are nonsquares
concepts.summary: A prime natural number cannot be a perfect square. If it were m², then m would be a divisor strictly between 1 and m².

groups.title: Apply the criterion to primes and to 2
